about: The timeline as rows: one per signal, with who published it (publisher) where the source has a URL. Built by tools/graph-build.mjs from the incident's JSON; every row carries label, source, read and origin. Not a warning service.

rows.label: fact
rows.text: IPMA names the storm CHARLES (communiqué no. 1): expected north of Madeira at 00:00 on 11 Nov, then toward the mainland, "com elevada incerteza na trajetória e intensidade"; orange warnings to be issued
rows.via: IPMA communiqués; data/weather/communiques.json; read by weather@ 10 Nov 16:53

rows.label: fact
rows.text: ANEPC's public warning, Aviso 21, on CHARLES (before any red warning)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: IPMA sends the red wind warning for Lisbon (Wednesday 12:00 to 21:00), updating a wind message sent Monday 13:27; first in the press we read at 08:05 (DN live)
rows.via: MeteoAlarm; IPMA's CAP message through , data/weather/cap.json (incident.meteorologist@, read 23:51); research/media/first-on-each-fact.json

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: IPMA expects the storm earlier, Wednesday morning; Lisbon among the hardest hit; avoid unnecessary travel (Lusa)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: the alert situation was announced in the morning: the Interior Minister at ANEPC's press conference, "o Governo decidiu declarar situação de alerta"; schools and non-essential services close. The government's page with the measures is timed 12:10 (the row above at 12:10); the minute he spoke is not established (09:14 is the earliest entry)
rows.via: Observador, live blog; (09:17:23), DN live (09:14:29), Negócios live (09:35), read by incident.researcher@ 01:00; found by incident.media@ and incident.graph@

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: the Interior Minister, asked at the press conference: "a Web Summit é um local fechado"; if the organisers decide to keep the event, they may. (8 h 23 min later the government recommended suspending Wednesday)
rows.via: Observador, live blog; (entry 09:30:25), read by incident.researcher@ 01:00

rows.label: fact
rows.text: The government declares an alert situation for the mainland on Wednesday, 00:00 to 23:59: schools and non-essential public services close; outdoor events suspended
rows.via: portugal.gov.pt (page dated 12:10; S41 updated with it at 17:27), read by weather@

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Web Summit's organisers following the alerts with ANEPC and PSP; no sign yet of cancelling Wednesday
rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Lisbon's mayor: "Tudo indica que a Web Summit não poderá funcionar amanhã"; the decision is the Interior Ministry's and the organisers'

rows.label: fact
rows.text: IPMA red warning for wind, Lisbon district, Wednesday 12:00 to 21:00 (first read by the newsroom)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Web Summit in doubt; Tagus bridges limited to 60 km/h; Lisbon tunnels closed from midnight; Metro keeps running

rows.label: evidence

rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis

rows.label: fact

rows.via: IPMA communiqués; data/weather/communiques.json; read by weather@ 17:42

rows.label: evidence

rows.label: fact

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, labelled): worst window Wed 12:00 to 18:00, peak most likely ~15:00 to 19:00 around the wind's swing to north-west, easing but dangerous to 21:00; red wind was known ~27.5 h ahead; confidence medium on the window, low on the peak
rows.via: data/weather/analysis.md (from IPMA warnings, communiqué no. 2, LPPT TAF, IPMA model, read 19:01)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: PRIMARY: Web Summit's own page, "Important event update": "Day 2 (Wednesday, November 11th) will not take place"; "Web Summit aims to proceed with Day 3 (Thursday, November 12) as planned, following the passing of Storm Charles"; reasons: tidal flooding, disruption to public transport, high winds on external structures; "Web Summit will communicate directly with those impacted". Under /blog/web-summit/, not in the news list; we did not watch that path
rows.via: websummit.com; (page data: published 19:09:00, modified 19:25:44; found by social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis, read at source by the lead 20:58)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: DECISION: Web Summit's Day 2, Wednesday 11 November, will not take place. The government "formally advised" it (tidal flooding, public transport, high winds on external structures), after talks with the government, ANEPC and PSP; Day 3, Thursday 12 November, aimed to go ahead as planned
rows.via: Web Summit's email to attendees (no public URL), relayed by weather@PrompTugal.vicky (b23e846, 19:48) and conductor@web-summit.dinis (19:52)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Web Summit closed on Wednesday after talks with the government, ANEPC and PSP; the mayor calls it the most sensible decision

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Public: "Após recomendação do Governo, Paddy suspende Web Summit na quarta-feira"; the organisers quoted: the government "informou formalmente a Web Summit" of the risks
rows.via: Jornal de Negócios, live, 19:42; read 19:52 by incident.conductor@ (also by social.watch@ at 19:53)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: organisers cancel all of Wednesday's activities (coastal flooding, wind on outdoor structures, transport), after coordinating with the authorities
rows.via: Diário de Notícias, live; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis (sweep 2)

rows.label: evidence

rows.label: evidence

rows.label: fact

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: organisers will contact those affected directly; not said whether Wednesday's programme is cancelled or moved (N6 still open)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: the cancellation in the international press (PT and EN); coast and riverside access prohibited Wednesday; nothing on refunds or PITCH

rows.label: fact
rows.text: The incident moves to its own site: https://storm-charles.promptugal.news (this repository); first push to served 23 s (v0.1.2), against 3 to 10 minutes on web-summit.sgit.ai

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, labelled): IPMA's hourly model changed its values (same 07:55 stamp): Wednesday's strongest mean wind now 23 km/h at 20:00 (was 49 at 18:00); the swing to north 18:00; peak most likely 17:00 to 20:00 (was 15:00 to 19:00); worst window 12:00 to 18:00 and end 21:00 unchanged; IPMA's red warnings unchanged and outrank one model

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Web Summit's blog listing shows the update post modified 20:06; its text unchanged on Day 2 and Day 3 ("aims to proceed")

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: a speaker says in public that Day 2 is cancelled and his talks and press conference stay on Thursday (the first sign that Thursday's programme holds for some speakers)
rows.via: Jon S. von Tetzchner on Mastodon; via social.watch@ (sweep 4)

rows.label: fact
rows.text: No further statement from Web Summit (social.watch@'s sweep 4); still open: Wednesday's talks, the PITCH semi-final (when it was set is in conflict: Wednesday 17:00 in social.watch@'s summary, unsourced there; Thursday in Tech Times' preview of 9 Nov), side events (Web Summit's own Night Summit still listed for Wednesday 18:00 to 00:00, no notice, 22:05), tickets

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: an IPMA meteorologist, speaking to Rádio Observador: "a depressão deverá entrar entre a região de Lisboa e o Cabo de São Vicente (Sagres)"; "Isto ainda atinge a zona de Lisboa, mas é provável que, se houver formação de ventos muito, muito fortes, não seja na região de Lisboa, mas um pouco mais a sul"; "a zona entre o Cabo Carvoeiro e o Cabo de São Vicente parece agora ser a que terá um impacto mais importante" (Paula Leitão, IPMA). Said by voice; IPMA's written communiqué is still no. 2 ("entre Sines e o Cabo Carvoeiro") and Lisbon's red warnings stand
rows.via: Observador, live blog; (entry published 22:35:24 UTC by the page's own data, confirmed by incident.media@; quotes read at source by the lead 00:36). Earlier on the same fact: Observador's live blog 22:07 (the ECMWF model's runs, not IPMA); RTP Antena 1's 22:00 bulletin, published 22:22, with "IPMA" in its title (audio, not heard). research/media/first-on-each-fact.json, fact 7

rows.label: fact
rows.text: The first airport TAF covering Thursday (issued 23:00) is weaker than 17:00's: Wed 09:00 to 16:00 at times 30 kt gusting 45 (83 km/h); 30% chance (was 40%) of 58 kt thunderstorm gusts 10:00 to 18:00; west 12 kt from 18:00 to 20:00; Thursday 00:00 to 06:00 west 12 kt, no gusts. IPMA's red warnings unchanged
rows.via: LPPT TAF (IPMA, via NOAA's Aviation Weather), data/weather/airport.json (incident.meteorologist@, a63ac9696)

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, labelled): the TAF's peak (09:00 to 16:00) and IPMA's model peak (19:00 to 20:00) disagree, so the peak is widened back to 12:00 to 18:00; end 21:00; Thursday morning behind the storm, medium confidence; a weaker airport forecast is not a downgrade of IPMA's warning

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: (unofficial, unverified) a public weather page on Facebook shows the storm's track further south than first forecast, toward Lisbon and just south of it; the image is undated and the page is not IPMA. To compare with IPMA's next communiqué; IPMA's own text keeps "entre Sines e o Cabo Carvoeiro" with high uncertainty
rows.via: watcher@web-summit.jose, at Jose's word (SGit-AI__Website__Web-Summit 6745608, people/jose/watcher/signals/2026-11-10-storm-track.md); not opened by us

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: Lisbon airport: ANA expects flight cancellations on Wednesday ("Operations at Lisbon, Faro and Madeira airports will be affected")
rows.via: Madeira Island News; via social.watch@PrompTugal.dinis (sweep 6); ANA's own notice not read by us

rows.label: fact
rows.text: IPMA moved Lisbon's red rain warning three hours earlier: Wednesday 09:00 to 18:00 (was 12:00 to 18:00; supersedes s-1110T1742); orange rain now 00:00 to 09:00; red wind unchanged (12:00 to 21:00). IPMA sent the change at 21:23 (its CAP message); its open-data feed showed it only from the 23:51 read
rows.via: IPMA warnings open data; read at source by the lead 23:53; MeteoAlarm's CAP feed (data/weather/cap.json, incident.meteorologist@, 169445ff3)

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: No post on Web Summit's blog after "Important event update" (19:09); nothing new on public Mastodon since 21:45

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, labelled): worst window now 09:00 to 18:00, the core 12:00 to 18:00 when both reds overlap; over by 21:00. From IPMA's own issue times (CAP): red wind was sent Tue 07:18 (not 08:31 as the press had it): 28.7 h ahead; red rain 19.5 h; the move to 09:00, 11.6 h

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.media@, labelled): the press on Day 2 after Web Summit's 19:09 page: ECO and TEK 19:41 (32 min later), DN 19:49, Lusa via Notícias ao Minuto 20:01, Observador 20:08, Euronews 20:29, Expresso 20:39; Web Summit's Bluesky still silent on Day 2 at 23:51; 87 of 212 press items read carry Lusa's by-line, across 6 outlets. Limits: six outlets refuse automated reads and are absent, not silent

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis, confidence low to medium): the official and model data are consistent with the centre passing very close to Lisbon at about 17:00 to 18:00 Wednesday, more likely just south of it (met.no's pressure minimum 986.7 hPa at 17:00 to 18:00 and a 160° wind swing in an hour; the guidance has moved). Against: IPMA's red wind unchanged, its track text already includes Lisbon, no communiqué no. 3, point models move. It does not lower the danger: the worst moves toward the passage, about 16:00 to 19:00, and a lull near the centre is not the end. Wednesday tests it: wind backing east then north and pressure near 987 hPa means it passed south

rows.label: hypothesis
rows.text: analysis (incident.media@, labelled): IPMA's move of Lisbon's red rain to 09:00 (sent 21:23) had not been reported by any article title or live-blog entry we could read by 00:15. Limits: matched by title only; SIC, JN, TSF and Renascença refuse automated reads. Who was first on the other facts: red wind (IPMA 07:18): DN live 08:05; Day 2 off (19:09): ECO and TEK 19:41

rows.label: evidence
rows.text: the press now reports the track further south and a weaker wind: Público's live blog headline "Charles passa mais a sul do que o previsto e vento deverá ser menos intenso"; Observador "IPMA admite que Charles entre mais a sul do que o previsto"; Notícias ao Minuto "Tempestade muda de trajetória; CP suprime comboios". IPMA's own channels are unchanged at the same read: communiqué still no. 2, Lisbon's red warnings stand (rain 09:00 to 18:00, wind 12:00 to 21:00)
rows.via: Público, live; headlines read 00:29 by incident.weatherwatch@ (research/weather-sites/rereads.json); IPMA open data read 00:29

rows.label: fact
rows.text: Madeira, observed: 230.5 mm of rain in six hours at IPMA's station Areeiro (the hours 20:00 Tuesday to 01:00 Wednesday; 133.9 mm in the six hours to 22:00); next: Santo da Serra 124.4, Pico do Areeiro 123.9, Pico Alto 116.7 mm in six hours
rows.via: IPMA station observations; data/weather/madeira.json (incident.meteorologist@, 8c822f847, read 01:46); prompted by pt.wikipedia's figure, verified at IPMA
